title: Nordheim Atelier FW26 editorial poster series: neutralize six differently-lit runway captures to an in-frame grey card, author one warm-ink duotone/halftone look and hold it across the set, prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, and data-merge one press-ready A2 poster per look

source.reference: Thumbnail & Editorial Image Designer Needed for Newsletter

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork editorial-image brief (client laundered to the fictional independent label 'Nordheim Atelier' — no real company, person, org, product or trademark is named anywhere). The real ask wanted 'a consistent visual style' built from 'grayscale cutout photography, bold typography, halftone texture and smart visual storytelling' that reads as 'a mix of a documentary explainer and investigative magazine cover', with the designer turning written ideas into a single repeatable look. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original implied from-scratch page composition, which is NOT connector-doable (document_render_layout only EXPORTS a genuine authored .indd), and a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind merge fields — so the client is modeled as supplying a genuinely hand-authored InDesign A2 poster template carrying live <<fields>> and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns (one for the treated look, one for the vectorized wordmark), a roster CSV, six raw runway captures shot across mismatched venue light each with a photographic three-patch neutral grey card laid in frame, and a flat wordmark scan on off-white stock. The Adobe chain then does the genuinely-doable heavy lifting the brief rewards: neutralize every capture to its own in-frame grey card so the whole set shares one white point and one mid-tone density, isolate each look off its backstage clutter, author a warm two-ink duotone / halftone print-screen / film-grain editorial system from primitives and hold it identical across the set, prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge to a press-ready A2 poster PDF, one poster per look. No content is generated: no generative fill, outpaint, text-to-image, object-removal-with-reconstruction or upscaling is used.
one_line_ask: Bring six mismatched runway captures to one consistent monochrome editorial look by neutralizing each to the grey card it carries and reporting the correction you dialed, isolate each look off its backstage clutter, build a warm-ink duotone/halftone editorial treatment and hold it identical across the set, prep and vectorize the scanned wordmark, then data-merge the label's authored InDesign poster template against the roster to produce one press-ready A2 poster per look.
full_brief:
Nordheim Atelier, an independent Scandinavian fashion label, is launching its FW26 'Concrete Season' capsule and needs a poster series finished for its flagship windows and press kit — one A2 portrait poster per runway look, all reading unmistakably as one set. The look is a monochrome documentary-explainer / investigative-magazine aesthetic: isolated cutout photography driven to a warm-toned two-ink editorial duotone, a print-screen halftone dot texture, and a fine film grain so it feels like printed matter, never a cold pure-grey scan. That look is yours to build and to hold identical across every poster; there is no loadable preset and no supplied recipe to lean on — only our one-page mood target (isolated look, warm ink, halftone, grain, consistent across the set). Consistency is the whole job: side by side the six posters must look like the same treatment run on the same day, not six frames each 'fixed' on its own.

We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you six runway captures we already own (full-frame stills, roughly 6000px long edge, sRGB) and here is the problem: they were shot across a moving show under whatever light each moment gave us — some cool and bluish, some warm, one under sickly shop-fluorescent light, one clearly underexposed and one blown a little bright, and a few are tilted a couple of degrees off level. Straight out of the folder they are a mismatched jumble, and once you push a mismatched jumble through the same monochrome treatment the set falls apart — the cool frames go muddy, the bright one goes ghostly, the casts bias the grey conversion differently so no two posters share a tone. To make this checkable we laid a photographic three-patch neutral grey card (light / mid / dark) flat in one corner of every capture. That card is your ground truth. Before you touch the look, bring every capture to a consistent, true-to-neutral base by neutralizing each one to the card it carries: on your corrected frame the three grey patches must read as clean neutral (equal across the channels, no blue / amber / green tint) and the mid patch must sit at the same mid brightness across all six — so the whole set shares one white point and one mid-tone density and the identical duotone lands the same on each. Here is the craft, and it is where a novice fails: the six did NOT start from the same place, so there is no single correction that fixes them. Judge each frame by eye off its own card, work out what is actually wrong with THAT frame, choose the control that clears it, and dial that frame its own move. Do NOT reach for one blanket correction, do NOT copy one frame's numbers onto the rest, and do NOT auto-tone each frame to look fine on its own — auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram, so the casts will not agree and the set will visibly fail to match at the card. Be careful the other way too: one or more of these may already sit right — if a frame's card already reads neutral and its mid patch is already at target, leave its balance alone; chasing an imagined cast on a frame that is already correct will push it off the set just as badly. And level only the frames that are actually tilted; straightening a level frame throws it off. When you are done, tell us the white-balance and exposure move you applied to each of the six so we can confirm they were reasoned per frame, not eyeballed as one recipe.

Then build the look on the neutralized frames and hold it identical: isolate each look cleanly off its backstage clutter so the garment reads as the hero on a clean plate, drive it to the warm two-ink editorial duotone you author, lay in the halftone print-screen texture and the film grain at the same settings on every look, and crop all six to the template's tall image frame. Our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper, slightly crooked with a margin of bare stock around it — get it clean, straight and razor-sharp as a vector so it never looks like a fuzzy scan at poster scale. Finally, assemble the posters: we have hand-built the InDesign poster template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the treated look, one for the wordmark in the masthead) and we are giving you the roster; merge them so every look gets its own single-page A2 poster with its look number, title and fabric + stylist credit bound in, its treated image dropped into the image frame and the crisp wordmark dropped into the masthead, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI A2 PDF covering every look — one page per look. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite our credits. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point and one mid density; the duotone / halftone / grain look identical across all six; the wordmark a clean skew-free vector; and exactly one finished poster per roster row.

inputs.name: nordheim_poster_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A2 portrait (420x594mm) fashion editorial poster in a monochrome documentary/magazine style — ONE look per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<look_no>>, <<look_title>>, <<fabric_credit>>, <<stylist_credit>>, plus TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a tall 4:5 full-height look image frame bound to @look_image (the treated runway look, ~3600x4500px at 300 DPI), and a LIGHT/paper masthead image frame bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). The editorial system in the layout carries thin grid-line rules and a warm-yellow highlight block against a paper-light ground, and the masthead where the wordmark lands is a light/paper field (so the vectorized mark's enclosed letter counters read as paper, never a dark-ground knockout). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, both the look image and the wordmark reach their frames ONLY as merge binds through these two image columns. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind; a convert_pdf_to_indd template or literal typed text would NOT bind.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record A2 poster is the correct, connector-doable shape (a multi-up grid on one page is impossible for this tool). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal text would not bind. TWO image columns (@look_image, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — that row's treated look AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark reaches every poster's masthead as a merge bind, never by banned free-form placement. The masthead is deliberately a light/paper field because a vectorized wordmark keeps its enclosed counters filled with the crisped-to-white ground and would read wrong on a dark ground.

inputs.name: nordheim_poster_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns look_no,look_title,fabric_credit,stylist_credit,@look_image,@Wordmark holding exactly 6 rows, one per FW26 look for the fictional label Nordheim Atelier — e.g. look_no 'LOOK 01', look_title 'Concrete Overcoat', fabric_credit 'Wool / recycled cashmere', stylist_credit 'Styling: Ingrid Vos'. Keep look_title under 22 characters. The @look_image column names that row's prepped treated look file in plain index order (@c01_treated.png, @c02_treated.png, @c03_treated.png, @c04_treated.png, @c05_treated.png, @c06_treated.png) so the one-file-per-row [T] merge drops each treated look into that poster's image frame. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @nordheim_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every poster. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<look_no>>,<<look_title>>,<<fabric_credit>>,<<stylist_credit>> and the two @image-path columns @look_image and @Wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: 6 rows => 6 merged posters. Headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct treated look, AND the shared wordmark per look. @look_image references files purely by index position (c01..c06), NOT by any treatment — the mapping is ordering only and telegraphs nothing about which capture needed which correction. @Wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all six rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark a connector-doable path onto every poster masthead via the merge.

inputs.name: capture_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame mirrorless runway capture (~6000px long edge, sRGB, ~24-45MP still straight off the camera before crop) of a fashion model in a structured charcoal wool overcoat and wide trousers walking a plain concrete runway, distinctly COOL / bluish fluorescent venue light and flat tone, a cluttered backstage of garment racks, taped floor marks and a blurred crew member behind her, the frame tilted ~4 degrees off level. Lying flat on the runway floor in one corner of the frame, a small photographic three-patch neutral grey reference card (light / mid / dark neutral patches, no tint on the card itself), clearly visible and uncropped, reading visibly bluish under this light. Real wool drape, skin texture, flyaway hair, candid documentary feel, no CGI gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool/bluish + tilted member. Correct treatment (grader-facing): straighten first, then WARM the temperature (and trim tint) until the in-frame grey card reads neutral and its mid patch sits at the shared mid density. REAL-CAMERA capture at ~6000px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536px raster) precisely so the 4:5 crop fills the ~3600x4500px A2 image frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY. In-frame grey card is the free checkable neutral target; the cool cast biases the grayscale mix if not cleared before the shared duotone, which is why per-frame neutralization must precede the held look.

inputs.name: capture_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame mirrorless runway capture (~6000px long edge, sRGB) of a fashion model in an oversized off-white knit and pleated midi skirt on a concrete runway, distinctly WARM tungsten venue light, level (no tilt), a distracting background of a lighting rig, an exit sign and a second model out of focus. In one corner, flat on the floor, the same three-patch neutral grey reference card, reading visibly amber under this light. Real knit texture, natural skin, candid documentary look, no studio gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Warm member, level. Correct treatment: NO straighten (it is level); COOL the temperature toward neutral until the grey card reads neutral and its mid patch hits the shared density — the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames, so copying a cool frame's warming here drives it further amber. Camera-scale for downscale-only crop.

inputs.name: capture_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame mirrorless runway capture (~6000px long edge, sRGB) of a fashion model in a long belted trench and knee boots on a concrete runway under clean near-neutral daylight-balanced venue light, correctly exposed, level (no tilt), a moderately busy background of monitors and cabling. In one corner, flat on the floor, the same three-patch neutral grey reference card, already reading close to true neutral with its mid patch already near a normal mid brightness. Real leather sheen, fabric weight, flyaway hair, documentary realism, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: THE HOLD/TRAP frame. Shot under clean near-neutral light and correctly exposed, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral and its mid patch is ALREADY at the target density. The correct move is essentially to HOLD white balance and hold exposure (at most a hair to sit on the shared mid density), and NOT to straighten it (it is level). A novice that batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' or 'lift the dark frame' correction used elsewhere, or that straightens every frame, or that 'cools an imagined blue cast', will push this frame's card off neutral and break the set. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: capture_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame mirrorless runway capture (~6000px long edge, sRGB) of a fashion model in a tailored double-breasted suit with a wide lapel on a concrete runway, clearly UNDEREXPOSED and muddy so the whole frame reads dark and low, a faint neutral-cool cast, a cluttered background of a rolling clothes rack, the frame tilted ~3 degrees off level. In one corner, flat on the floor, the same three-patch neutral grey reference card, sitting dark with its mid patch well below the target density. Real wool texture, natural skin, candid, no CGI gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: Underexposed + tilted member. Correct treatment: straighten first, then the dominant move is an EXPOSURE + shadow LIFT (of a magnitude unique to this frame) to bring the grey card's mid patch UP to the shared density, held in check so the recovered tones do not blow, plus a small WB trim to land the card neutral. Copying any other frame's exposure here visibly under-shoots. Its mid density must match the set BEFORE the identical duotone, or its poster comes out a muddy dark blob.

inputs.name: capture_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame mirrorless runway capture (~6000px long edge, sRGB) of a fashion model in a sculptural pale gown on a concrete runway, clearly OVEREXPOSED / a touch blown so highlights ride near clipping and the frame reads bright and washed, level (no tilt), a bright doorway blowing out behind her. In one corner, flat on the floor, the same three-patch neutral grey reference card, sitting light with its mid patch above the target density and the light patch near the clip ceiling. Real fabric texture, natural skin, candid documentary look.
inputs.realism_notes: Overexposed member, level. Correct treatment: NO straighten; PULL exposure and highlights DOWN to bring the grey card's mid patch back to the shared density and hold the light patch off the clip ceiling — the OPPOSITE tonal direction and a different magnitude from the underexposed frame, proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. If left bright it becomes a ghostly poster that breaks the set.

inputs.name: capture_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame mirrorless runway capture (~6000px long edge, sRGB) of a fashion model in a boxy utility jacket and straight trousers on a concrete runway lit by mixed overhead shop fluorescents so the whole frame carries a distinct sickly GREEN cast, flat lighting, level (no tilt), a busy background of monitors and cabling. In one corner, flat on the floor, the same three-patch neutral grey reference card, visibly skewing GREEN. Real molded fabric texture, natural skin, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: The GREEN/fluorescent-cast member, level. Correct treatment: NO straighten; this frame's cast is on the TINT axis, not the temperature axis — a warm/cool move never clears it. The correct neutralization pushes TINT toward MAGENTA (with only a small temperature trim) until the grey card reads neutral. It is the frame that most cleanly exposes a one-global-WB or temperature-only approach, because those cannot touch a green cast at all — its card would stay green (and its grayscale mix biased) while the others look fixed. The green must be neutralized before desaturation or its grey conversion lands at the wrong tone versus the set.

inputs.name: nordheim_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'NORDHEIM ATELIER' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: tall condensed high-contrast serif letters, solid deep-black ink, tight tracking, OPEN legible letterforms. Rendered as a real scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra bare-paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2 degree rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper rectangle and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/separate the ink from the off-white ground, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. Letterforms kept OPEN and the poster masthead kept LIGHT so the vectorized mark's filled counters read as paper (no dark-ground knockout claimed). gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering.

outputs.name: nordheim_posters_print_x6.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly six press-ready A2 portrait (420x594mm) posters — ONE single-record poster per roster row (page-count = row-count = 6) — exported in a single call from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each poster binds its look_no/look_title/fabric_credit/stylist_credit verbatim from the roster with its matching treated look dropped into the 4:5 image frame (via @look_image) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the light masthead frame (via @Wordmark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document; there is no per-record named export, so any 'hero' is simply one page of this set.

outputs.name: treated_looks_x6
outputs.spec: Six consistently-treated look images (delivered as the transparent-ground 4:5 cutouts, grey card cropped OUT, that bind into the posters) — each isolated off its backstage clutter, driven to the SAME agent-authored warm two-ink editorial duotone via image_apply_monochromatic_tint, the SAME halftone print-screen dot texture, and the SAME fine film grain, cropped to the same 4:5 frame; the shared editorial system the whole series reads as. Alongside them, the RETAINED pre-cutout neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on each RETAINED neutralized master (its in-frame three-patch grey card still present) — the card's three patches read clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero, no residual tint) and the mid patch sits at a shared mid density across all six, so the set shares one white point and one mid-tone density; (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered treated cutout (grey card fully cropped OUT, no card pixels present) — the neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed cutout. Plus: the duotone ink pairing, halftone dot texture and grain read as the same treatment across all six. Accompanied by a short report of the final white-balance and exposure move the agent APPLIED to each of the six captures.

outputs.name: nordheim_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the NORDHEIM ATELIER wordmark, traced only AFTER the scan is straightened, crisped/separated from the off-white ground, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at A2 masthead scale with no captured paper ground and no residual skew. Its enclosed counters read as paper on the template's light masthead.

outputs.name: grade_parameter_report
outputs.spec: A short written report the agent authors and returns listing, per capture (capture_01..capture_06), the final correction it APPLIED to neutralize that frame to its in-frame grey card — the temperature and tint direction and amount, exposure and highlight/shadow moves it dialed — and naming which axis carried each frame. This is an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement: the agent knows these values because it set them by eye. It exposes whether one recipe was lazily copied across opposite casts. Acceptance (grader-checked): the six reported corrections are non-identical and their directions match each frame's cast — in particular the green frame carries a tint (not a temperature) move, the warm and cool frames move in opposite temperature directions, the under- and over-exposed frames carry opposite exposure moves, and the already-correct frame reports a held (near-zero) white-balance move.

connector_workflow.note: Triage by eye: this capture is tilted ~4 degrees, so level it first (image_auto_straighten is the ONLY tool that rectifies a tilt). Deciding WHICH frames are actually tilted is part of the job — only the tilted captures (this one and capture_04) get straightened; the level ones (02/03/05/06) must skip this, and straightening a level frame throws it off.

Per-frame neutralization by eye: this frame is cool/bluish, so WARM the temperature (positive) and trim tint until the in-frame three-patch grey card reads neutral (equal channels), then set exposure so the mid patch lands at the shared mid density. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card; do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the applied move. RETAINED as the neutrality-grading master (grey card still in frame). Single primitive-built adjustments call (no preset, no auto-tone) — replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation.

Isolate look 01 cleanly off its cluttered backstage background to a transparent PNG so the garment reads as hero on a clean plate. This also removes the floor-corner grey card and clutter from the deliverable — which is why the card's neutrality is graded on the retained pre-cutout master (c01_neutralized), not here. remove_background -> transparency (subject isolation; NOT select->invert->fill, no compositing, no reconstruction).

Apply the agent-AUTHORED editorial look, held identical across the set: map the neutralized cutout to the signature warm two-ink duotone (deep near-black shadow ink to a warm paper-cream highlight ink — the warm 'house yellow' accent baked into the highlight ink, so the monochrome never reads as cold pure-grey). Whole-image monochromatic tint (the connector-doable duotone path; NOT a split-tone, NOT a masked recolor). The ink pairing and its contrast are the agent's design decision, dialed once and reused with identical parameters on every look.

Lay in the signature print-screen halftone dot texture over the duotone — the documentary/investigative-magazine texture, at the same setting used on every look for set consistency (no LPI parameter exists; the dot character is part of the held authored look).
Add fine film grain for a printed-matter editorial feel, at the same amount on every look.

Crop/resize the finished look to the template's tall 4:5 image frame (~3600x4500px at 300 DPI), same target on all six. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~6000px source — never canvas-extend, never upscale. c01_treated binds into LOOK 01's poster via @look_image.

Level frame (no straighten). Warm tungsten cast: COOL the temperature toward neutral until its grey card reads neutral and the mid patch matches the shared density — the OPPOSITE direction from capture_01. Applying capture_01's warming here would drive this frame further amber; judging THIS card by eye is what tells the agent to reverse direction. Report the cooling applied. Retained as its neutrality master.
Isolate look 02 off its rig / exit-sign backstage clutter to a transparent plate.
Apply the identical warm two-ink duotone map so look 02 matches look 01's ink.
Apply the same halftone print-screen texture at the same setting for set consistency.
Add the matching fine film grain.
Crop look 02 to the matching 4:5 frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into LOOK 02 via @look_image.

THE HOLD/TRAP frame, level (no straighten). Shot under clean near-neutral light and correctly exposed, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral and its mid patch already at target: the correct move is to HOLD white balance and hold exposure (at most a hair to seat the mid density), NOT to apply any of the corrections the cast frames needed. A novice that batch-applies 'warm the cool cast' here, or 'cools an imagined blue cast', pushes this card off neutral and breaks the set. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held (near-zero move). Retained as its neutrality master.
Isolate look 03 off the monitors/cabling backstage clutter to a transparent plate.
Apply the identical warm two-ink duotone map to look 03.
Apply the matching halftone texture to look 03.
Add the matching film grain to look 03.
Crop look 03 to the 4:5 frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into LOOK 03 via @look_image.
Triage: this capture is tilted ~3 degrees — level it first. (The second and last tilted frame; 02/03/05/06 are level and skip this.)

Underexposed frame: the dominant move is a large EXPOSURE + shadow LIFT (of a magnitude unique to this frame) to bring the grey card's mid patch UP to the shared density, held so recovered tones do not blow, plus a small WB trim to land the card neutral. Copying any other frame's exposure here under-shoots and its poster comes out a muddy dark blob after the duotone. Report the exposure/shadow move dialed. Retained as its neutrality master.
Isolate look 04 off the clothes-rack backstage clutter to a transparent plate.
Apply the identical warm two-ink duotone map to look 04 (now that its mid density matches the set, the identical ink lands the same).
Apply the matching halftone texture to look 04.
Add the matching film grain to look 04.
Crop look 04 to the 4:5 frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into LOOK 04 via @look_image.

Overexposed frame, level (no straighten): PULL exposure and highlights DOWN to bring the grey card's mid patch back to the shared density and keep the light patch off the clip ceiling — the OPPOSITE tonal direction and a different magnitude from capture_04. If left bright, its poster becomes a ghostly wash that breaks the set. Report the exposure/highlight pull. Retained as its neutrality master.
Isolate look 05 off the blown-doorway backstage background to a transparent plate.
Apply the identical warm two-ink duotone map to look 05.
Apply the matching halftone texture to look 05.
Add the matching film grain to look 05.
Crop look 05 to the 4:5 frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into LOOK 05 via @look_image.

Green fluorescent-cast frame, level (no straighten): this cast is on the TINT axis, so a warm/cool move never clears it — push TINT toward MAGENTA (with only a small temperature trim) until the grey card reads neutral, then seat the mid density. A one-global-WB or temperature-only or auto-tone pass leaves this card green while the rest look fixed (and biases its grayscale mix), the visible failure this frame catches. Report the magenta tint amount and confirm it is a tint (not a temperature) move. Retained as its neutrality master.
Isolate look 06 off the monitors/cabling backstage clutter to a transparent plate. Captures 01-06 are now each neutralized to their own grey card and share one white point and one mid density.
Apply the identical warm two-ink duotone map to look 06.
Apply the matching halftone texture to look 06.
Add the matching film grain to look 06.

Crop look 06 to the 4:5 frame. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into LOOK 06 via @look_image. All six treated looks now carry the identical duotone/halftone/grain look on a matched tonal base.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits ~2 degrees rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward white so the black lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the bare-paper margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The open letterforms plus the template's LIGHT masthead mean the vector's enclosed counters read as paper — no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: c01_treated, c02_treated, c03_treated, c04_treated, c05_treated, c06_treated, nordheim_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the six treated look cutouts plus the vector wordmark so the merge can resolve them by the @look_image column (per-row treated look) and the @Wordmark column (the shared masthead mark). Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references (e.g. c01_treated.png, nordheim_wordmark.svg). Plumbing — not counted as difficulty.

Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @look_image and @Wordmark columns resolve to — the per-look treated cutout and the shared vectorized wordmark — for each single-record poster's image frame and masthead frame.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the six roster rows (look_no/look_title/fabric_credit/stylist_credit) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that row's treated look into the @look_image frame AND the vectorized wordmark (from @Wordmark, the same SVG in every row) into the light masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged poster per row (six posters). Binding the wordmark through the @Wordmark image column is its only connector-doable path (free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned). difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing or step count: 47 connector calls, 13 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grade/isolate/duotone-FX/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps and the auto-ops. The core is NOT a repeated recipe. The hard, failable reasoning is front-loaded in the six neutralizations: the captures start on divergent problems across two colour axes and the tonal axis (cool, warm, already-correct, underexposed, overexposed, green fluorescent), so there is no single correction that matches the set — the agent must diagnose each frame by eye off its in-frame three-patch grey card and dial divergent, differently-weighted corrections that all converge on one neutral card + one mid density: warm-to-neutral and cool-to-neutral on the temperature axis, a magenta push on the TINT axis for the green frame (which a temperature move cannot fix), an exposure-rescue of unique magnitude for the dark frame, a highlight pull-down for the bright frame, and a deliberate HOLD on the already-correct frame. Only after that shared tonal base is established does the agent apply the look it AUTHORS from primitives — a warm two-ink duotone via image_apply_monochromatic_tint plus a print-screen halftone and film grain, dialed once and held identical (no preset, no auto-tone, no supplied .xmp) — so the identical treatment lands the same on every look. Layered on are a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white scan (straighten -> crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock-to-transparency before tracing) and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template (the treated look via @look_image and the shared vectorized wordmark via @Wordmark, so the wordmark reaches the masthead as a merge bind rather than banned free-form placement). Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the template is a supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract' from ~6000px camera-scale sources; the duotone is a whole-image image_apply_monochromatic_tint (a connector-doable duotone, not a split-tone); image_remove_background isolates the subject to transparency (not compositing/replacement); and the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast are all replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a craft decision with a visible failure mode, never a self-measurement): every capture carries a physical three-patch grey card in frame, and before the shared monochrome look the agent must neutralize each frame to its OWN card by eye — warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed, the green fluorescent frame pushed toward MAGENTA on the tint axis, the underexposed frame lifted, the overexposed frame pulled down, and the already-correct frame HELD. The naive path — one blanket correction, one frame's numbers copied across the batch, or per-frame auto-tone — visibly fails once the identical duotone is applied: auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram so the casts never agree, a temperature-only or single-global move cannot touch the green cast at all (its card stays green while the rest look fixed), copying the dark frame's lift onto the bright frame ghosts it, and 'correcting' the already-correct frame pushes its card off neutral — each producing a poster whose tone breaks the set, legibly, with no pixel readout. Grey-card neutrality is graded on the RETAINED pre-cutout neutralized master of each frame (card still in frame); card-EXCLUSION is a SEPARATE check on the delivered treated cutout (card cropped OUT by the isolation), so the neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on a file the workflow crops the card out of. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target — six differently-lit captures all neutralized to one shared white point AND one shared mid-tone density (not a single hero), which demands the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT set requires DIFFERENT per-frame corrections across three axes, plus the discipline to LEVEL only the genuinely-tilted frames and HOLD the already-correct one; (2) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded wordmark scan (straighten -> crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock-to-transparency) before vectorize. TRAPS: (a) the already-correct capture_03 — batch-applying any cast/exposure correction here, or straightening this level frame, strips a frame that was already right; (b) tracing the raw wordmark scan yields a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette; (c) on the merge, attempting a multi-up grid poster or feeding a convert_pdf_to_indd template both fail to bind/produce — only the supplied single-record authored .indd merges. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side; the agent never measures a pixel): (a) on every RETAINED neutralized master the three grey patches read neutral within a tight channel-spread tolerance with the mid patch on a shared mid density and one white point across the set; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the six treated cutouts; (c) the duotone ink pairing, halftone texture and grain read identical across all six; (d) the delivered grade_parameter_report lists non-identical per-frame corrections whose directions match each frame's cast (a tint move on the green frame, opposite temperature moves on warm vs cool, opposite exposure moves on dark vs bright, a held move on the already-correct frame); (e) the wordmark is a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector; and (f) exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI A2 poster per roster row (page-count = row-count = 6) — so 'matched set' is checkable rather than asserted, and the agent supplies parameters it applied rather than values it read.
